newsitem.title: UK: EBRD in $90mln deal with Lafarge for East Europe.
newsitem.headline: EBRD in $90mln deal with Lafarge for East Europe.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is to provide a $90 million equity investment for France's Lafarge Copee to develop the region's cement and building materials sector.
"It will provide much needed equity finance to a highly cyclical and capital intensive industry," Jacques de Larosiere, president of the EBRD, said in a statement.
The first joint venture investment will be in the Kujawy plant in Poland.
The total cost of the Polish project will be $145.2 million, of which the EBRD said it will contribute up to $34 million.
The Kujawy cement plant near Poznan has an annual production capacity of 1.2 million metric tonnes.

"By supporting Lafarge's planned investment in cement and other building projects in central and eastern Europe, the EBRD's multi-project facility will have an important transition impact," de Larosiere said.

The EBRD's contribution to the program will take the form of a 30 percent stake in the capital of Lafarge Polska, a holding company for all of Lafarge's majority shareholdings in Poland, Lafarge said.
The French company has a 25 percent share of the Polish cement market and owns plants in Malogoszcz and Wierzbica. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
